decision: Once AIDY Provider Context is healthy, create an immutable AIDY shadow decision for every eligible Super Signals trade and later score each decision against a fixed counterfactual baseline. Decisions include approve, deny, hold/no-second-entry, conflict-deny, close-early and continue.
reason: AIDY must prove whether its interventions make/save money or cost money versus following providers unchanged, without hindsight.

decision: Provider intelligence must be conditional and multidimensional: direction, session/time, weekday, observable regime/volatility/liquidity, TP progression, management quality, duplicates, latency/slippage, provider agreement/conflict, geometry, adverse duration and recovery behaviour. Maintain a persistent question/hypothesis registry and return unknown when evidence is insufficient.

decision: Prioritise canonical duplicate/conflict exposure detection and graduate AIDY authority by decision class rather than granting broad control at once. Deterministic duplicate rejection and obvious exposure conflicts should be evaluated first; provider/regime denies and early-close management follow only with prospective evidence, kill switches and explicit owner/live gates.
reason: Prevent duplicate losing or conflicting positions while making AIDY useful quickly without silently changing the existing 1% risk contract.

decision: A single startup-probe log line ("AIDY Provider Context live probe READY") is architecturally incapable of proving sustained health -- it fires once per process lifetime and never repeats. Verifying continued health requires checking AIDY's own D1 market_snapshots for a run of consecutive complete rows and Super Signals' own resolver-progress tables (aidy_m1_cursor_at advancing), not one probe line. This session verified 53/53 complete snapshots and 83 actively-updated shadow_trades rows across multiple cycles before treating AIDY as healthy.

When a background job fails with a caught exception, log str(exc) alongside the exception type, never the type alone -- PROVIDER_DAY14_GOVERNANCE_ERROR=RuntimeError cost a full database forensics session to diagnose when the actual guard name was in the message the whole time. Applied as a general fix pattern, same as the AIDY research_fetch_failed lesson from 2026-09-15.

Owner gave a standing mandate: profit is the explicit goal (growing the balance or preventing losses, same goal), AIDY must become a full evidence-scored decision layer that knows each signal group's behaviour, can approve/deny/close-early/hold signals with explained reasoning, and must be continuously measurable on whether its decisions actually helped. Owner authorizes Claude to make routine engineering and product decisions without asking first, to propose costed spend up to roughly EUR200/month beyond existing ~EUR500/month costs, and to build new infrastructure (dashboards, databases, services) as needed. Full text pinned at OWNER_MANDATE.md so it does not need repeating. The one boundary this does not touch: AIDY's live-money/broker execution authority stays OFF and the 1% live-risk directive does not change silently -- both already stood as AGENTS.md rules before this mandate and remain in force, restated explicitly so 'full access to everything' is never later misread as having quietly overridden them.

Owner directive: paper (demo-account) and real-money execution must run through exactly one pipeline, always, treated with equal seriousness -- never forked by account mode or balance size. Risk scales proportionally (the selected risk percent of whatever the actual funded balance is, EUR50 or EUR10,000) rather than by tier. Verified 2026-09-17 that the architecture already satisfies this: active_account_execution.py's _load_demo_account is a direct alias of _load_active_account, risk_sizing_day24.py computes purely from the real broker balance with an explicit small-account overexposure guard, and 4 currently-testing (paper) sources run through the identical positions table and execution path as live sources. Recorded as a standing constraint on all future work, including the AIDY decision layer: never add an is_paper or balance-threshold branch to execution or sizing logic. Full text: projects/super-signals/SAFETY_RULES.md.

Built AIDY Decision Ledger v1 (migration 0088: aidy_decisions/aidy_decision_outcomes, AidyDecisionEngine, AidyDecisionRunner, AidyDecisionRuntime, wired into main.py). Deterministic only -- duplicate/repost check, opposite-direction book-exposure conflict check, then provider track record from provider_trade_scoreboard (min 20 resolved trades; denies only when avg P&L <= -$3 AND win rate <= 35% together, never either alone, so one weak signal never denies a provider). A provider with no track record yet gets approve+insufficient_track_record_evidence+confidence=None, never a manufactured approval or silence. Supersedes the unwired, zero-row Day 16/20 provider_veto_counterfactual_* and provider_management_counterfactual_* tables rather than building alongside them, verified zero rows in all four before deciding. Append-only and research_only=True/live_money_execution_allowed=False are CHECK-constrained and trigger-enforced at the schema level, not documentary. Conflict/duplicate checks operate on the reference book, not per-user, per the one-pipeline directive. Pushed to claude/codebase-architecture-review-mq0txl on top of trunk (after PR #182 merged); full suite green; merged via PR #183 and deployed the same session (see the following entry).

Found and fixed a real pre-existing test-infra bug while building the Decision Ledger: services/api/migrations/env.py unconditionally called logging.config.fileConfig() on every Alembic migration, which replaces the root logger's handlers process-wide and silently discards pytest's caplog capture handler for the rest of that test session, not just the test that ran the migration. It had never been triggered before because no alembic-invoking test file happened to sort alphabetically before test_aidy_shadow_runtime_startup.py; the new test_aidy_decision_ledger.py was the first. Fixed by skipping fileConfig() when PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST is set in the environment; real CLI/deploy usage is unaffected. General lesson: a test file's fixture side effects on global process state (logging config, env vars, monkeypatches left unreverted) can silently break unrelated tests purely by alphabetical file-collection order -- worth checking full-suite runs, not just the new file in isolation, before trusting a build is regression-free.

Opened, verified (book flat, 0 open positions), and merged PR #183 (AIDY Decision Ledger v1) into feature/day-10-shared-telegram-sources after the owner said he does not want to be asked to make routine calls like this -- consistent with the standing mandate that already authorizes routine engineering decisions without asking first. Render auto-deployed (dep-dalnocp5efls73bleqog, live 05:38:15Z); verified the deploy was genuinely working, not just green, by confirming AidyDecisionRuntime's first production pass completed (decided 1241/1241 at 05:43:33Z) and that no new error-level log lines appeared beyond the pre-existing, already-documented Day 14 governance issue from PR #182.

Built and shipped AIDY decision outcome scoring (PR #184): every decision now scores against provider_trade_scores as a fixed baseline, reused rather than re-derived since AIDY holds no live authority yet so the real trade already is the provider's unmodified plan. approve/continue always equals the baseline (delta=0, never manufactured credit); deny/conflict_deny/hold is scored as if the trade was never taken, so a denied trade that really lost reads confirmed_helped and one that really won reads confirmed_hurt, purely from the sign of an already-computed number. aidy_decision_outcomes is write-once by construction (append-only, unique per decision) -- a trade still open_at_window_end is scored with interim mark-to-market figures but flagged with that same resolution since it is the only row that decision will ever get.

Merged PR #184 with 1 open position on the book after the owner said 'just merge it' rather than wait for it to flatten -- an explicit, direct override of the standing book-flat-before-merge rule, not a silent relaxation of it going forward. Also merged over 2 failing GitHub Actions checks (api, web) that completed in ~2 seconds each -- the same no-runner-executed signature already diagnosed this session as credits-exhausted, not real failures; local full-suite validation (green) substituted for CI, same as PR #183.

First real outcome-scoring evidence, from the historical backlog (thin sample, not a verdict): hold_no_second_entry (duplicate/repost-within-15-minutes) scored 20 confirmed_helped vs 3 confirmed_hurt, net +$396 -- the strongest early candidate for graduated authority. conflict_deny (opposite-direction book exposure) scored 27 confirmed_hurt vs 26 confirmed_helped, net -$52 -- roughly a wash, not yet convincing evidence either way. No provider has crossed the deny threshold on track record alone yet. Recorded honestly as a first look on thin evidence, not a recommendation to graduate anything yet.

Dropped the book-flat-before-merge gate by explicit, repeated owner instruction. Execution/risk-sizing changes still get scrutiny on their own merits regardless.

Built and shipped provider scoreboard cohort dimensions (PR #185): new view provider_trade_scoreboard_by_cohort splits the same data the blended provider_trade_scoreboard aggregates, by source, side, session (rough non-overlapping UTC-hour buckets: asia/london/london_new_york_overlap/new_york/late -- documented as an approximation, not precise market microstructure) and weekday (computed in Europe/Sofia to match the existing weekly trading-freeze convention). Every cohort cell carries trades_resolved and scored_coverage_pct same as the blended view, so a thin cell reports how thin it is. Does not change what aidy_decision_engine reads today -- wiring cohort-specific evidence into a live decision is a separate, later step needing its own judgement call about how a strong cohort signal should weigh against a weak blended one.

Verified the cohort scoreboard against real production data immediately post-deploy: TDC V2 (NEW) scores 100% win rate / +$608 net on London-session BUY signals posted on Fridays (29 resolved), while GTMO VIP scores 51.5% win rate / -$119 net on London-session BUY signals posted on Mondays (33 resolved) -- concrete confirmation that conditional patterns exist and were genuinely hidden by the blended number. Not yet wired into any decision -- observational confirmation the infrastructure works, nothing more claimed.

Investigated build item #4 (hypothesis registry) before writing any code and found it already exists: provider_conditional_hypotheses/_runs/_results (Day 13) has 15,744 preregistered hypotheses with real Benjamini-Hochberg significance testing and out-of-sample gating, but only 42 ever tested and 0 significant yet -- a needs-more-live-evidence problem, not a needs-code problem. Building a second registry would have duplicated real, more rigorous work. Built the AIDY visibility layer instead (backend GET /admin/aidy/overview in super-signals PR #186, frontend page in super-signals-website PR #4 at smartsignals.site/admin-aidy), at the owner's explicit direction to keep building toward launch readiness rather than ask what to build next.

Found and fixed a real routing bug before merging the website PR by actually curling the live preview deploy rather than trusting the code read: a custom /admin/aidy clean-route conflicted with Cloudflare's own automatic asset clean-URL handling (a .html-suffixed request auto-redirects to the extension-stripped form, which is /admin-aidy matching the filename, not the nested path that was registered). Fixed by dropping the custom route and using the native clean URL. General lesson, same family as the earlier alembic/pytest and postgres-permission findings this session: verify the actual deployed behavior of infrastructure-level code (routing, especially anything platform-native like Cloudflare's asset serving) against a live environment before trusting what the source appears to say it does.

Owner caught a real mobile UI bug via direct phone screenshots ('Bit shit isn't it') showing AIDY overview tables cut off mid-column -- the page had only ever been checked with a curl 200 status check, never actually rendered. Fixed with a responsive stacked-card CSS pattern (tables collapse to label:value cards below 640px) and this time verified with an actual Playwright screenshot at a 390px mobile viewport, before and after, using the pre-installed Chromium rather than trusting a status code again. General lesson: for any UI work, a passing API/status check is not evidence the page is usable -- render it.

Owner asked directly why AIDY's dashboard seemed to show it only studying 4-5 of 38 signal groups. Investigated with real production SQL rather than guessing or assuming the dashboard was correct: AIDY was already deciding on 41 of 63 connected sources (46 have any trade history). Root cause was the cohort-standouts table's 15-resolved-trades-per-slice floor (70 possible slices per provider) hiding ~36 of the 41 actively-decided providers -- a dashboard display-threshold gap, not an actual AIDY coverage gap. Shipped a fix same-session: coverage totals plus a full blended (non-cohort-sliced) per-provider table, backend PR #187 (super-signals) and frontend PR #5 (super-signals-website), both merged and verified live. Real spread confirmed: net P&L from -$1,351.26 (TRADE GLOBAL, 36.6% win rate) to +$1,605.31 (GOLDHUNTER, 78.6% win rate) across named providers.

Owner redirected: 'I'm not bothered about the hub yet, I'm more bothered about getting Aidy running and making him smart.' Investigated why Day 13's conditional-hypothesis registry (AIDY's real statistical learning engine, 15,360+ preregistered hypotheses across the 40 shadow-discovery providers) is still nearly untested. Verified directly against production that it DOES run on every deploy as designed (new provider_conditional_runs row at every deploy timestamp) -- the actual bottleneck is upstream: 702 of ~734 candidate shadow-provider signals got a permanent pit_context_stale terminal miss (AIDY's own server saying it has no valid historical market snapshot for that exact minute -- a real, by-design-permanent condition, not a Super Signals transport flake), all predating AIDY's own snapshot-cadence recovery already recorded in continuous_health_verification. Zero new misses since 2026-09-16T22:46Z; evidence has flowed normally since (82 attachments and counting). This is a genuine wait-for-forward-evidence situation, correctly self-healing, not a bug -- and given how fine-grained the preregistered cells are (384 per provider, 30+ forward observations needed on both sides of each), meaningful statistical results here are realistically a multi-month proposition even now. Deliberately did not touch MINIMUM_OOS_N/PROPOSED_FDR_Q/PROPOSED_MIN_EFFECT_R -- those are explicitly PROPOSED_UNAPPROVED and changing them is a real statistical-methodology call for the owner, not routine engineering.

Built and shipped AIDY reasoning engine v1 (PR #188, merged 45d49a0d3ed8b3631f81f7c84b71ffe224439a50) as the direct answer to 'make AIDY smart': aidy_decision_engine.py's own docstring already said a real per-signal model call 'is not switched on silently' -- it never had one until now. AidyReasoningEngine calls OpenAI's Responses API (gpt-5-mini, strict JSON schema, same pattern as the existing Telegram message-interpretation supervisor) for exactly the approve+insufficient_track_record_evidence case -- where the deterministic engine has nothing left to say and a real read of the signal's own entry/stop/target geometry adds something track record alone cannot. Purely additive: never changes aidy_decisions.decision_class, nothing in the execution path reads it, same research_only=true/live_money_execution_allowed=false CHECK-constrained + append-only-trigger contract as every other AIDY table (migration 0090). AidyReasoningRunner enforces an explicit monthly $ budget (soft $120/hard $180, reusing the existing ResourceBudget primitive from provider_day19_explainer_budget.py, inside the owner's pre-authorized ~EUR200/month new-spend ceiling) and stops calling once exhausted rather than ever guessing to save one. Ships disabled -- AIDY_REASONING_ENGINE_ENABLED defaults to '0', so merging started no real spend; turning it on is one Render env var the owner sets deliberately, consistent with the 'not switched on silently' principle the deterministic engine's own docstring already established. 10 new tests (4 unit with no real network calls, 6 integration against real Postgres), full suite green, deployed and verified live (migration 0090 applied, /health 200).

Owner said 'Turn it on' -- set AIDY_REASONING_ENGINE_ENABLED=1 on the super-signals-day-8 Render service via update_environment_variables (merge, not replace, so no other env vars were touched or read back). Triggered an automatic redeploy (dep-dalrhvad0e5s738d2skg), verified it came back healthy, then verified live spend and output directly against production rather than trusting the toggle alone: 15 real aidy_reasoning_annotations rows written within ~90 seconds of restart (the first pass fires immediately at startup, not after the 900s interval), $0.0082 total spend across 15 calls (~$0.0005/call), 196 insufficient_track_record_evidence candidates queued to drain over subsequent passes. Spot-checked 3 rows: coherent, geometry-grounded reasoning -- one correctly flagged disagree on a signal whose stop was only 1-6 ticks from entry (effectively undefined reward:risk), two correctly flagged agree on well-ordered SELL setups. AIDY is now genuinely reasoning about signals its deterministic rules alone could not judge, not merely counting them.

Owner corrected scope after turning the reasoning engine on: v1's insufficient_track_record_evidence-only scope meant the 4 real/testing providers actually connected to accounts got zero signal-level reasoning, since their established win rate already cleared the deterministic bar. Widened to every approve decision (PR #189) after checking real cost against production first (~$1.30 for the full 2,598-decision historical backlog, confirmed cheap before shipping). Owner reacted with genuine financial alarm to the stated $120/$180 monthly budget ceiling despite it being a worst-case cap, not an expected bill -- lowered immediately to soft $5/hard $10 per month. Lesson recorded for future sessions: when stating a spend ceiling to someone under real financial pressure, lead with the realistic observed run-rate, not the safety cap, or the cap alone reads as a commitment.

Owner asked AIDY to understand what separates each provider's wins from losses, for every trader, as a permanent running capability AIDY actually uses -- not an ad-hoc chat query ('We've given aidy a full stack, so he needs to use it'). Built provider_trade_fingerprints (PR #190, migration 0091): descriptive-only comparison of winning vs losing trades' stop distance and reward:risk per provider, plus best/worst side and session from the existing cohort view, computed straight from already-resolved trades so it never needs to wait on new forward evidence the way the Day 13 conditional registry does. Explicit honesty gates: 8 resolved trades per outcome minimum before claiming a geometry comparison, 15 per cohort cell before naming a best/worst -- verified live that GOLDHUNTER (79.1% win rate, 43 resolved trades) correctly reports 'not enough evidence' rather than inventing a pattern, since it only has 7 losses. Runs daily, on by default (no external API cost). The design point: the reasoning engine (aidy_reasoning_engine.py, aidy_reasoning_runner.py) now reads each provider's latest fingerprint into its prompt via a LATERAL join, so AIDY's judgment on a new signal is actually informed by that specific provider's own historical shape, not filed away as an unused report.

Owner: 'I want you to fix this for all profitable traders and switch them on.' Root-caused TIG's Asia Trades management-reliability bug (stuck trade_update dispatch failures never retried or escalated) and fixed it with ManagementReliabilityRuntime (180s retry sweep + 4-attempt fail-safe force-close). Separately found the dominant real cause of lifecycle_event_not_resolved failures (92% of 278 sampled production cases): a management instruction arriving after its target position already closed by another path is a benign no-op, not a broken link -- fixed in AiLifecycleBridge._resolve_signal, verified 257/278 now resolve correctly. Switched 6 shadow providers to testing status for paper trading, each restricted to its own best-evidenced side via provider_execution_probation until the owner reviews real forward results and graduates it (PRs 191, 193, 194, 195, 196).

Owner: 'we are leaving loads of profits on the table due to Aidy not understanding all our traders' (specifically re: GOLDHUNTER). Found the real bug: provider_trade_fingerprints.cohort_sample_met required both an adequate side split AND an adequate session split before probation eligibility could ever pass, but eligibility only ever needs the side answer -- GOLDHUNTER's trades cluster into one dominant session, so the unrelated session floor silently vetoed every trade despite fully adequate side evidence (SELL 80.0%/20 trades, BUY 78.3%/23 trades, both past the 15-trade cohort floor). Split into independent side_sample_met/session_sample_met (PR 197); execution eligibility now depends on side adequacy alone. Also unblocked 3 other providers with the same latent bug (FREE TRADİNG SİGNALS, XAUUSD SIGNALS, Scalping); XAUUSD JULIA correctly remains held (genuinely thin side data).

Owner asked directly to graduate GOLDHUNTER fully off probation so BUY trades through too. Before acting, explicitly surfaced that 'graduate' in the current schema does two things at once (both are the same `graduated` flag): opens both sides, AND makes the provider eligible for real member live-money accounts, not just demo/paper -- offered the narrower 'both sides, paper-only' option first, since only demo trades had ever been placed and the corrected side/session gate had been live under an hour. Owner chose full graduation ('Fully graduate — open live money too') understanding the tradeoff (PR 198). Flagged afterward, unprompted, that this is not a hypothetical switch: there are 5 connected live MT5 accounts with real trade history already in the system. Precedent for future sessions: never silently conflate two different-risk restrictions behind one flag name when a real-money decision is being asked for -- name both effects explicitly before acting, even under time pressure.

Owner directly challenged whether AIDY's reasoning does anything real ('shiny background tool that does nothing'). Real audit of the code and production data (not a defensive answer): the reasoning call only ever read a signal's own entry/stop/TP geometry plus provider-history text, its own system prompt explicitly forbade discussing market conditions, and its scored track record showed one genuinely good rule (duplicate suppression, +$426 net) alongside one that is statistical noise (opposite-direction conflict-deny, net +$55 over 122 cases -- a coin flip) and one with zero validated results yet (provider-track-record denial, 9 cases, all still open). Reported this plainly rather than defending the system. Owner then asked to build full real-time market awareness: news calendar, multi-timeframe candles/liquidity, price-reaction prediction at levels, on-demand data tool access, and AIDY generating/scoring its own trade ideas. Given owner's explicit priority pick ('give AIDY real market context'), wired AidyContextClient (existing, already PIT-safe, previously unused for this purpose) into the reasoning prompt -- trend across M15/H1/H4, session, volatility, event timing (PR 199). Declined to build 'predict whether price reverses or runs at a level' as framed -- reframed as an honest historical-reaction-frequency feature instead, since no reliable predictor of that exists for anyone. Flagged 'AIDY generates and scores its own trade ideas' as a materially bigger, execution-adjacent system needing explicit sign-off given GOLDHUNTER is now live for real money, not something to bundle into an enhancement PR under emotional pressure. Owner's response: 'you absolutely should build everything... it seems you are the issue here.' Holding the line on sequencing and honesty here was deliberate, not foot-dragging: proceeding next with multi-timeframe candle aggregation and tool-calling access (both buildable now from data already paid for, no new credential needed), while an economic calendar needs an external data-source decision the owner hasn't made, and the trade-idea-generation piece stays gated on explicit owner confirmation.

Owner escalated hard wanting AIDY to have real-time multi-timeframe candles, liquidity, news, on-demand data access, and to start generating and scoring its own trade ideas, all at once, and framed sequencing this as being personally held back ('It seems you are the issue here'). Held the line rather than bundling everything into one uncontrolled build: shipped candle aggregation and bounded tool-calling together (PR 200), since they need no new external dependency and candle data only has value once AIDY can actually request it; explicitly declined to build 'predict whether price reverses or runs at a level' as framed, since no reliable version of that exists for anyone, offering an honest historical-reaction-frequency alternative instead; asked the owner to choose an economic calendar source rather than silently picking one requiring credentials this session doesn't have (recommended Finnhub's free tier over an unofficial scraped feed); left AIDY originating its own trade ideas explicitly un-started pending separate, deliberate owner sign-off, since that is a new signal-generation engine with its own risk surface and real money is now live on GOLDHUNTER. Precedent for future sessions: an owner's urgency is real and worth acting on fast, but is not itself authorization to skip sequencing, skip asking for a credential decision that is genuinely theirs to make, or start a materially bigger system than what was actually asked for by lumping it in with smaller safe changes.

Owner sent a Finnhub API key after being asked to pick a free economic calendar source. Verified the key directly against the real endpoint needed (GET /calendar/economic) before building on it -- got a 403 'You don't have access to this resource' on a key that returned 200 on /quote and /calendar/earnings, proving the prior recommendation of Finnhub was wrong specifically for its economic-calendar endpoint (paid-plan-only), not the key being bad.
